notes: ONE PLACE TO RECONCILE AGAINST THE BANK. The Reconciliation screen used to have two ways to read a statement — its own quick import, which matched by amount alone, and a separate Bank Statements screen. They did the same job, so they are one now. Import statement on the Reconciliation screen reads the bank PDF (text or scan), Excel or CSV, checks the running balance on every row, and puts every line the bank printed on screen. The separate Bank Statements menu entry is gone and nothing it held is lost: the lines, the learned rules and the imported statements are all under Statement lines on the Reconciliation screen. The Cheque and Lodgement Register remains the manual path for a month with no statement to upload. MATCH, POST, IGNORE — SAID ON THE SCREEN. Every line the bank printed stays on screen until you say what it is. MATCH: it is one of your own cheques or lodgements, marked presented or credited on the BANK date through the register own path. POST: the ledger never saw it (a charge, interest, a fee), booked as the reconciliation own adjustment voucher on the bank date. IGNORE: not a ledger item at all, set aside with a note. Each has its undo. WHY DOES NOT IT BALANCE. When the reconciliation is out, a new button beside the difference runs the checks an accountant runs in their head, on the figures already on screen, and names what would explain the whole difference, most likely first: one open statement line that equals it (a charge to post, a receipt to match); one register item that equals it (a cheque the bank has already paid); two or three open lines that add up to it; an item counted on both sides; two digits swapped somewhere; a slipped decimal. Each comes with what to do. When nothing fits it says so, and says what to check next. A SEARCH BOX ON THE GENERAL LEDGER THAT READS WHAT YOU TYPE. One box. An amount (1,500 or 1500.00) finds a debit or credit of exactly that; ~1500 finds within one per cent; >1000, <500 and 1000-2000 are ranges. A date (03/08/2026), a month (Aug 2026, or August alone) or a bare year finds the entries of those days. A voucher code or a cheque number finds its entries; a word finds it in the narration, the voucher, the account, the unit or the project; a quoted phrase must appear exactly; -word leaves those out; dr or cr keeps one side. Every term must hold, the totals foot what is shown, and the print and the Excel export say they are a search result. The running balance is hidden while searching, because a balance over a subset is not a balance of anything. STATEMENTS THAT FOLLOW ON. When a statement is checked, the app now says whether it follows on from the last one imported for that account. Bank statements open where the previous one closed, so a gap between them means a statement in between is missing, or the bank own figures disagree with themselves — named at the import, not found at year end. RULES THAT SET A LINE ASIDE. A line you set aside every month — a bank own balance line, an internal sweep the ledger books elsewhere — can be remembered: tick Remember this when you set it aside, and the next line whose narration carries the pattern is proposed as set aside, one click. ALSO FIXED SINCE THE LAST FEED: a cheque cannot be marked cleared on a date before it was written — the bank date is checked against the register and refused with both dates, never written. A posted charge now moves the cashbook figure on screen at once. ONE SMALL DATA CHANGE: the rules table now admits a rule with nothing to post. This installs straight over the previous version. Please still take a backup first: Backup & Export, Back up now.
